questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'CANDID'.
questions.solution: 'Candid' means frank and honest. Its opposite is 'Devious' (deceitful, evasive). 'Blunt', 'Honest' and 'Forthright' are all synonyms or near-synonyms of candid, not opposites.

questions.question: Pointing to a photograph of a woman, a barrister said: 'Her daughter is the only granddaughter of my mother.' If the barrister has no sisters, how is the woman in the photograph related to the barrister?
questions.solution: The barrister's mother's only granddaughter (with no sisters) must be the barrister's own daughter. The woman whose daughter is the barrister's daughter must be the barrister's wife.

questions.question:
Statements:
1. All treaties are binding agreements.
2. No binding agreements are unilateral declarations.
Conclusion:
I. No treaties are unilateral declarations.
II. Some treaties are unilateral declarations.
Which conclusion logically follows?
questions.solution: Treaties ⊆ Binding Agreements. Binding Agreements ∩ Unilateral Declarations = ∅. Therefore, Treaties ∩ Unilateral Declarations = ∅. Only Conclusion I ('No treaties are unilateral declarations') is definitively valid.

questions.question: A person travels 12 km North, turns right and travels 5 km. How far and in which direction is he from his initial starting position?
questions.solution: Displacement = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 km. Direction is North-East.

questions.question: A cooperative society increased the price of fertilizer by 25%, and later decreased the new price by 20%. The net percentage change in price is:
questions.solution: Net multiplying factor = 1.25 × 0.80 = 1.00. Since the factor is exactly 1, there is no net change in price (0%).

questions.question: Two investment funds, Alpha and Beta, yield annual compound returns of 17% and 16% respectively. If an institutional endowment invests ₹10,00,000 divided between the two funds such that both investments yield identical total interest after 2 years (with annual compounding), what is the ratio of capital invested in Fund Alpha to Fund Beta?
questions.solution: Let capital be C1 and C2. Total interest after 2 years is C1 × [(1 + r1)² - 1] = C2 × [(1 + r2)² - 1]. Therefore C1/C2 = [(1 + r2)² - 1] / [(1 + r1)² - 1] = 0.3456 : 0.3689.

questions.question: Five fertilizers — P, Q, R, S and T — are ranked strictly by their nitrogen content, from highest to lowest. Q has more nitrogen than R but less than S. T has less nitrogen than R. P has the highest nitrogen content of all, more than S. Which fertilizer has the FOURTH-highest nitrogen content?
questions.solution: From the clues: P > S > Q > R > T. Counting from the highest: 1st P, 2nd S, 3rd Q, 4th R. Hence R has the fourth-highest nitrogen content.

questions.question:
A square sheet of paper (side 6 cm) is folded twice: first along its horizontal line of symmetry (bottom edge onto top edge), then along the new vertical line of symmetry (right edge onto left edge), producing a 3 cm × 3 cm folded square.
[Figure description: After the two folds, the folded square's four corners correspond respectively to the four quadrant-corners of the original sheet, EXCEPT for the one corner that lies at the intersection of both fold lines, which corresponds to the exact centre of the original sheet. A circular hole of diameter 1 cm is punched at precisely this centre-corresponding corner of the folded square.]
When the paper is unfolded, the sheet shows:

options.A: One circular hole at the centre of the sheet
options.B: Four separate circular holes, one near each corner of the sheet
options.C: A single circular hole at one corner of the sheet
options.D: Two circular holes, one on each half of the sheet

questions.solution: The punched corner lies exactly at the intersection of both fold lines, which is the single point corresponding to the centre of the original sheet (unlike the other three corners of the folded square, which map to four distinct quadrant corners). Reflecting this single point through both folds still gives just one point — the centre. Hence unfolding produces one circular hole at the centre of the sheet, not four separate holes.

questions.question: A feed mix contains maize and soybean meal in the ratio 7:3 by weight, totalling 150 kg. If 15 kg of maize is removed and 5 kg of soybean meal is added, the new ratio of maize to soybean meal becomes:
questions.solution: Total parts = 7+3 = 10, so 1 part = 150/10 = 15 kg. Maize = 105 kg, Soybean meal = 45 kg. After the changes: Maize = 105 − 15 = 90 kg, Soybean meal = 45 + 5 = 50 kg. New ratio = 90:50 = 9:5.

questions.solution: Let capital be C1 and C2. Total interest after 2 years is C1 × [(1 + r1)² - 1] = C2 × [(1 + r2)² - 1]. Therefore C1/C2 = [(1 + r2)² - 1] / [(1 + r1)² - 1] = 0.3689 : 0.2100.

questions.question: For a soil sample, the relationship between void ratio (e) and porosity (n) is given by:

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: In watershed management, constructing small check dams / gully plugs across first-order drainage lines is primarily intended to:

options.B: Reduce flow velocity, trap sediment, and control gully erosion

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Check dams and gully plugs reduce the velocity of concentrated flow in small drainage lines, causing sediment to settle behind the structure and arresting further gully head-cutting/widening — a core soil-and-water-conservation practice in watershed management.

questions.question: Waterlogging in irrigated agricultural land is primarily caused by:

options.B: Rise of the water table due to over-irrigation and poor drainage

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Waterlogging occurs when the water table rises close to the root zone, typically due to excess irrigation water combined with inadequate natural or artificial drainage, restricting soil aeration and root respiration.

questions.question: Which of the following are objectives of agricultural drainage?

options.A: Lowering the water table to a safe depth
options.B: Removing excess soil salts through leaching
options.D: Increasing capillary rise of groundwater into the root zone

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Drainage aims to lower the water table, facilitate salt leaching, and improve aeration/trafficability. Increasing capillary rise of groundwater into the root zone would worsen waterlogging/salinity and is the opposite of a drainage objective, so option D is incorrect.

questions.question: In grain drying, the period during which the drying rate depends on the internal moisture diffusion rate rather than on surface evaporation conditions is the:

Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): During the falling rate period, surface moisture has largely been removed, and drying is governed by the rate at which moisture diffuses from the grain interior to the surface, so the drying rate falls with time.

questions.question: Kick's Law of size reduction states that the energy required is proportional to:

options.B: The logarithm of the size reduction ratio (Dp1/Dp2)
options.C: The square root of the particle diameter
options.D: The cube of the particle diameter

Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:

• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Kick's Law states E = K_K ln(Dp1/Dp2) — the energy required is proportional to the logarithm of the ratio of the initial to final particle size, reflecting energy needed to achieve a given size-reduction ratio regardless of absolute particle size.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding material-handling equipment used in agricultural processing are correct?

options.A: Bucket elevators are used for vertical conveying of granular materials
options.B: Screw conveyors are suited for handling powdery or granular materials over short-to-medium horizontal distances

Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.

Hammer mills are SIZE-REDUCTION equipment (they use impact to break down material), not material-handling equipment, so option D is incorrect.

questions.question: A cylindrical grain bin of diameter 5 m and height 5 m is filled to 75% of its volume with grain of bulk density 720 kg/m³. Find the mass of grain stored (in tonnes), rounded to two decimal places.

• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.

questions.question: A lot of maize weighing 1500 kg is at 18% moisture content (wet basis) and is to be dried to 14% (wet basis) for safe storage. Find the mass of water to be removed (in kg), rounded to two decimal places.

questions.question: For f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 1, the value of x at which f has a LOCAL MAXIMUM is:
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): f'(x) = 3x² − 12x + 9 = 3(x−1)(x−3), so critical points are x=1 and x=3. f''(x) = 6x−12. At x=1: f''=−6<0 → local maximum. At x=3: f''=6>0 → local minimum. Hence the local maximum occurs at x=1.

questions.question: For the matrix A = [[3,1],[1,3]], find the sum of the squares of its eigenvalues.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Trace = 6, Determinant = 9−1 = 8. Characteristic equation: λ² − 6λ + 8 = 0 → (λ−2)(λ−4) = 0 → λ = 2, 4. Sum of squares = 2² + 4² = 4 + 16 = 20.

questions.question: Solve dy/dx = 3y with y(0) = 2. Find y at x = (ln 3)/3, rounded to two decimal places.

• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): General solution: y = 2e^(3x). At x = (ln3)/3, 3x = ln3, so e^(3x) = 3. Hence y = 2 × 3 = 6.

questions.question:

questions.question: An air-standard diesel cycle has a compression ratio r = 16 and cut-off ratio ρ = 2. Using γ = 1.4, the theoretical thermal efficiency (in %) is given by η = 1 − (1/r^(γ−1))·[(ρ^γ − 1)/(γ(ρ−1))]. Find η, rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): r^(γ−1) = 16^0.4 = e^(0.4×ln16) = e^1.109 = 3.031. ρ^γ = 2^1.4 = e^(1.4×ln2) = e^0.970 = 2.639. Bracket term = (2.639−1)/(1.4×1) = 1.639/1.4 = 1.171. η = 1 − (1/3.031)×1.171 = 1 − 0.386 = 0.614 = 61.4%.

questions.question: For a watershed of area 25 hectares, the rainfall intensity is 60 mm/h and the runoff coefficient is 0.5. Using the Rational Formula Q = CiA/360 (Q in m³/s, i in mm/h, A in hectares), find the peak discharge (in m³/s), rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Q = (0.5 × 60 × 25)/360 = 750/360 = 2.08 m³/s.

questions.question: Water flows through a pipe of diameter 200 mm at a velocity of 1.5 m/s. It enters a second pipe of diameter 125 mm. Using the continuity equation, find the velocity (in m/s) in the second pipe, rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): By continuity, V₂ = V₁(D₁/D₂)² = 1.5 × (200/125)² = 1.5 × 2.56 = 3.84 m/s.

questions.section: Section 4: Soil and Water Conservation Engineering
questions.question: A venturimeter has an inlet diameter of 250 mm and a throat diameter of 100 mm. The piezometric head difference between inlet and throat is 0.8 m. Taking g = 9.81 m/s² and neglecting losses, find the velocity at the throat (in m/s), rounded to two decimal places, using continuity together with Bernoulli's equation between inlet and throat.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Area ratio gives V₁ = V₂/(D₁/D₂)² = V₂/6.25 (since (250/100)²=6.25). Bernoulli: (V₂²−V₁²)/2g = 0.8. Substituting V₁²=V₂²/39.0625: V₂²(1 − 1/39.0625) = 2×9.81×0.8 = 15.696 → V₂²×0.9744 = 15.696 → V₂² = 16.11 → V₂ = 4.01 m/s.

questions.question: A soil has a field capacity of 30% and a permanent wilting point of 14% (both on a weight basis). The bulk density of the soil is 1.3 g/cm³. Find the total available water in the top 0.5 m of soil depth (in mm).
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Available water fraction = 30% − 14% = 16% = 0.16. Total available water = 0.16 × 1.3 × 500 mm = 104 mm.

questions.subtopic: Irrigation Water Conveyance and Application Methods
questions.question: An irrigation channel must carry a discharge of 1.5 m³/s. Using Manning's equation Q = (1/n)·A·R^(2/3)·S^(1/2), with n = 0.02 and bed slope S = 0.0009, and given that for this channel's trapezoidal cross-section at the design condition the flow area is A = 3y² and the hydraulic radius is R = 0.75y (both given directly, so no iteration is needed), find the normal flow depth y (in m), rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): S^0.5 = √0.0009 = 0.03, and 1/n = 50. Q = 50 × 3y² × (0.75y)^(2/3) × 0.03 = 4.5 × (0.75)^(2/3) × y^(8/3). Now (0.75)^(2/3) = e^[(2/3)ln0.75] = e^(−0.1918) = 0.8256. So Q = 4.5 × 0.8256 × y^(8/3) = 3.715·y^(8/3). Setting Q=1.5: y^(8/3) = 1.5/3.715 = 0.4038. y = 0.4038^(3/8) = e^[(3/8)ln(0.4038)] = e^(−0.340) = 0.712 m.

questions.question:
A tube well fully penetrates a confined aquifer of thickness 12 m and hydraulic conductivity 25 m/day. Pumped at a steady rate, the drawdown at the well is 2.5 m and at an observation well 40 m away it is 0.6 m. Using the Thiem equation Q = 2πKb(s₁−s₂)/ln(r₂/r₁), with well radius r₁ = 0.1 m and r₂ = 40 m, find the discharge Q (in m³/day).
Agricultural Process Engineering (from Q.29)
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Q = 2π × 25 × 12 × (2.5−0.6)/ln(40/0.1) = 2π × 300 × 1.9/ln(400) = 3581.4/5.991 = 597.8 m³/day.
Agricultural Process Engineering

questions.question: Paddy weighing 800 kg at 24% moisture content (wet basis) is dried to 13% moisture content (wet basis). Find the mass of water removed (in kg), rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Dry matter = 800 × (1−0.24) = 608 kg. Final mass = 608/(1−0.13) = 608/0.87 = 698.85 kg. Water removed = 800 − 698.85 = 101.15 kg.

questions.question: A single-effect evaporator concentrating fruit juice evaporates 350 kg/h of water. The steam economy of the evaporator (kg water evaporated per kg steam supplied) is 0.85. Find the steam consumption (in kg/h), rounded to the nearest whole number.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Steam consumption = Water evaporated/Steam economy = 350/0.85 = 411.76 kg/h.

questions.question: Crushing a material from an average diameter of 25 mm to 8 mm consumes 10 kJ/kg, following Rittinger's Law E = K_R(1/Dp2 − 1/Dp1). Find the additional energy (in kJ/kg) required to further reduce the material from 8 mm to 3 mm, rounded to two decimal places.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): First find K_R: 10 = K_R(1/8 − 1/25) = K_R(0.125−0.04) = K_R × 0.085 → K_R = 117.65. For 8 mm → 3 mm: E = 117.65 × (1/3 − 1/8) = 117.65 × (0.3333−0.125) = 117.65 × 0.2083 = 24.51 kJ/kg.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about homogenization of milk are correct?

options.A: Homogenization reduces the average size of fat globules
options.B: Homogenization reduces/prevents cream separation (creaming) during storage
options.C: Homogenization is typically carried out by forcing milk through a narrow valve/orifice at high pressure
options.D: Homogenization increases the fat content of milk

questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Homogenization mechanically breaks down fat globules into smaller, more uniformly dispersed droplets (by forcing milk through a narrow valve at high pressure), which reduces creaming during storage. It does not add or remove any fat — the fat content of the milk is unchanged, so option D is incorrect.

questions.question: Milk flowing at 1500 kg/h through a heat exchanger is cooled from 40°C to 5°C. The specific heat of milk is 3.9 kJ/(kg·°C). Find the heat removal rate required (in kW), rounded to one decimal place.
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Mass flow rate = 1500/3600 = 0.4167 kg/s. Heat removal rate Q = m·cp·ΔT = 0.4167 × 3.9 × (40−5) = 0.4167 × 3.9 × 35 = 56.9 kW.

questions.question: The decimal reduction time (D-value) of a bacterial spore at 121°C is 1.8 minutes. A canning process is designed to achieve 10 decimal reductions (log₁₀(N₀/N) = 10) at 121°C. Using log₁₀(N₀/N) = t/D, find the required heating time (in minutes).
questions.solution:
Multi-Chain Solution Workflow:
• Step 1 (Governing Principles & Inputs): Analyze parameters.
• Step 2 (Chained Formulations): Substitute values into the primary governing relation.
• Step 3 (Evaluation & Unit Conversion): Heating time t = D × log₁₀(N₀/N) = 1.8 × 10 = 18 minutes.
